title: Connection-thinning and staged KV degradation playbook for downstream resilience
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: During cross-region incidents and downstream store slowdowns (Redis/Kafka/Postgres), the serving runtime experiences connection pile-up, long tail latencies, and cascading failures. We need an operationally simple, measurable playbook that systematically thins connection churn, stages KV/cache degrations, and provides predictable multi-region failover behavior so customer-facing SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency and availability) remain acceptable.

Scope: connection pool policies, adaptive timeouts, staged cache/kv degradation modes (read-only, stale-reads, TTL-override), per-tenant admission controls, hedging/soft-fallback to regional replicas, and circuit-breaker behavior tied to SLIs. This ticket captures design, decision log, implementation notes, rollout strategy, and runbook snippets for on-call ops.
acceptance_criteria: Connection thinning implemented: dynamic max_conns and backoff windows configurable per region and per pool
Staged KV degradation modes available and toggleable: NORMAL -> STALE_READS -> READ_ONLY_CACHE -> BYPASS_KV
Circuit-breaker thresholds wired to 95th/99th latency and error-rate SLIs with automatic open/half-open flow
Per-tenant soft admission and priority lanes configured; low-priority tenants are shed gracefully under overload
Multi-region hedging that falls back to regional replica within 50ms additional latency budget
Dashboards show SLIs, per-pool connection count, queue length, and degradation mode; SLO alerts suppress noisy paging using hysteresis
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose staged degradation over immediate hard-fail to preserve degraded correctness for high-value tenants (decision by runtime PM and infra leads).
2026-03-03: Use percentile-based circuit-breaker triggers (p95/p99) instead of simple error counts to account for tail latency regressions (proposal from reliability team).
2026-03-05: Implement connection thinning (reduce active connections by probabilistic eviction) rather than force-closing all idle sockets to avoid TCP RST spikes (network team input).
2026-03-07: Hedge to regional replica when origin latency exceeds adaptive threshold; hedging policy is probabilistic for low-risk traffic to limit load on failover replicas.
implementation_notes: Add adaptive_conn_limit per pool: base_limit * load_factor * tenant_priority_multiplier. Implement an exponential cooldown after conn limit hits that reduces accept rate by 10% each cooldown step.
Introduce 'degrade_state' metadata on route config: values [NORMAL, STALE_READS, READ_ONLY_CACHE, BYPASS_KV]. Degrade_state exposed via control-plane API and Console toggles.
KV degrader runs per-shard and supports TTL-override: when set, GETs can return items up to TTL+staleness_window and writes can be downgraded to async persistence.
Circuit breaker: monitor p95 latency and error-rate. Open CB when p95 > threshold AND error-rate > X% for sliding window. Use 'half-open' with tokened probe traffic at 1% of normal throughput.
Admission controller: per-tenant token buckets for request admission. Low tier tenants get 'best-effort' lane and are probabilistically shed when queue length > QLEN_THRESH.
Connection thinning: on high-queue, reduce new connection acceptance with a sampled drop probability computed from queue length and recent SLO breach counts.
Hedging: implement regional hedging at the framework level with configurable extra latency budget. Hedge only idempotent or read-path requests by default.
Metrics: instrument conn_accepts, conn_rejects, queue_length_histogram, degrade_state, stale_reads_rate, cb_state, hedged_requests, per-tenant_shed_rate.
Telemetry: ensure tracers tag 'degrade_state' and 'conn_thin_trigger' so traces reveal why a request was downgraded.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Deploy connection thinning and CB instrumentation to canary fleet (5% of runtime nodes) and collect metrics for 48h.
Phase 1 (limited): Enable staged KV degradation for internal traffic and non-critical tenants. Monitor stale_reads_rate and correctness regressions for 7 days.
Phase 2 (regional): Enable hedging and adaptive timeouts in us-west and europe regions with feature flags toggled by region.
Phase 3 (global): Gradual rollout to all regions with tenant-priority based defaults. Ramp down conservative knobs while monitoring p99 and error SLOs.
Rollback criteria: any sustained increase in production p99 latency > 15% or error-rate increase > 2% absolute for 30 minutes triggers automatic rollback to previous runtime config.
metrics_and_slos: SLIs to monitor: request_latency_p50/p95/p99, kv_get_success_rate, kv_get_stale_rate, conn_open_rate, conn_reject_rate, hedged_success_delta
SLOs (example): customer-facing p95 < 300ms, p99 < 800ms (90-day rolling). Availability > 99.9% for 'hosted-api' paths. Degraded mode acceptable if p99 < 1.2s for 5% of traffic in recovery windows.
Alerting: create SLO burn-rate alerts and a synthetic 'degrade-mode' alert that notifies infra but silences pager for transient automatic degradations under configured hysteresis.
runbook_steps: 1) Detect: Dashboard shows rising conn_reject_rate and p99 latency. If conn pool exhaustion is observed, set pool to 'thinned' mode via control-plane toggle.
2) Throttle: Trigger per-tenant admission with lowest priority lanes shed first. Notify Support and affected customers via internal dashboard.
3) Degrade KV: Move route to STALE_READS for affected shards; monitor correctness via shadow validation job for 10 minutes.
4) Hedge: Enable regional hedging for affected routes with low extra-latency budget. Observe hedged_success_delta metric to confirm improvement.
5) Recover: Once p99 returns within SLO for 30 minutes and conn queue drains, step-down degrade_state back to NORMAL in staged increments.
6) Post-mortem: Capture event in incidents Confluence page, include timeline, root cause, and improvements (e.g., pool sizing, better pre-warm on deployments).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Stale reads cause correctness regressions for stateful customers. Mitigation: Only enable STALE_READS for read-mostly keys and run shadow validation against a percent of traffic.
Risk: Hedging increases load on replicas and causes overload cascade. Mitigation: Hedge probabilistically and cap hedged concurrency to a small multiplier of normal capacity.
Risk: Misconfigured circuit-breaker opens too eagerly and reduces capacity. Mitigation: Use multi-signal triggers (latency + error-rate) and a conservative half-open probe strategy.
Risk: Connection thinning triggers client TCP retries leading to increased client-side latency. Mitigation: Prefer accept-drop (reject at protocol layer) with clear Retry-After headers for SDKs.
Risk: Too many feature flags increases complexity. Mitigation: Consolidate runtime flags into a single 'resilience-mode' with clear operator documentation.
